45.0.s.en: (1) Joseph makes himself known to his brothers

45.0.0.en: After the feelings of love that Judah showed in his readiness to redeem his brother Benjamin, that is, to become a slave in his place, because Jacob could not bear the separation from his youngest son, Joseph's feelings burned more within him, and he could not hide himself any longer. So he cried out to all the Egyptians standing before him to go out and leave him alone with these men. Then he began to weep so loudly that the Egyptians standing outside the doors heard him. Then he spoke in Hebrew and said to his brothers, "I am Joseph your brother," and he asked about his father, to whom his soul was attached. His brothers were terrified by the shock of the surprise, and they gave no answer, and even drew back in their fright.

45.1.0.en: With tears running from his eyes, Joseph asked his brothers to come near to him and not to be afraid of him or troubled because of their first sin of selling him as a slave to Egypt, because it was God who allowed this so that he might store up grain and they might not perish together, but He would feed them so that they might live. For two years of the famine had passed and five more years remained.

45.1.1.en: Joseph felt that the purpose of his mission to Egypt was to preserve the life of his family, and not his reaching a high position. Always think that the events of life that pass over you are a divine arrangement for the salvation of your own soul and of those around you whom you serve, so that you may lead everyone to the knowledge of God. Do not think about material things, for they pass away, nor about yourself and your dignity, but understand the will of God, which is the salvation of souls.

45.2.0.en: A father to Pharaoh: that is, responsible for managing all the affairs of the kingdom and caring for the matters of Pharaoh himself.

45.2.1.en: The land of Goshen: it lies east of the Delta in the present governorate of Sharqia. It was fertile land next to the desert and suitable for grazing.

45.2.2.en: Joseph told his brothers to tell his father of his great position in Egypt, and that he had authority over all its affairs and the management of Pharaoh's palace and all his matters. He asked that his father hasten to come, he and all the family, so that he might settle them in the land of Goshen, give them food, and care for all their affairs, because the famine would continue for five more years, and so that Joseph might enjoy being near his father.

45.3.0.en: He said to them, you see me and hear my voice, that is, you perceive the great reality in which I live, so tell my father all that you have seen and bring him quickly.

45.4.0.en: Joseph embraced his brother Benjamin, and the two wept, because he was his full brother. Then he kissed the rest of his brothers as a declaration of his pardon and forgiveness for all that they had done to him. They were reassured, and then they began to speak with humility, love, and joy in him.

45.4.1.en: Here Joseph's love for his father and his brothers appears, for greatness and glory did not make him forget to care for them, but he felt that the purpose of all this glory was to make his family happy.

45.5.s.en: (2) Pharaoh invites Joseph's family to Egypt

45.5.0.en: The Egyptians who worked with Joseph told Pharaoh of the coming of Joseph's brothers to him and that his father and the rest of his family still lived in Canaan. He rejoiced at this news and welcomed them to Egypt, and even commanded Joseph to bring all his family to dwell in Egypt and to send them wagons drawn by oxen in which to ride and come quickly, and not to be troubled about the land of Canaan, which they would leave, with any possessions of theirs there, because he would compensate them for it with all the abundant good things of Egypt. Although Joseph was the ruler and commander in all Egypt, Pharaoh relieved him of embarrassment in caring for his family and assured him of his welcome to them, for they were not foreigners, since they were his family.

45.5.1.en: If you please God, He will give you favor in the eyes of those around you, so that they care for you and for everything connected with you, and His good things to you increase spiritually and materially, and He compensates you for every loss.

45.6.0.en: Three hundred pieces of silver: that is, three hundred shekels of silver, and the shekel is about 15 grams.

45.6.2.en: Joseph carried out Pharaoh's orders, and his brothers got ready to go to Canaan to bring their father, and Joseph gave them gifts, which were:

45.6.3.en: 1- Changes of raiment for all his brothers, which is a sign of honor.

45.6.4.en: 2- He honored Benjamin more than them, because he was his full brother, so he gave him five changes of raiment and three hundred pieces of silver.

45.6.5.en: 3- He sent his father a gift, which was ten donkeys laden with the good things of Egypt and ten she asses carrying grain, bread, and various foods.

45.7.0.en: Before they departed, Joseph charged them not to quarrel on the way, each one accusing the other of being the cause of the wrong done to him when he was with them in Canaan, but to rejoice in the grace of God and thank Him.

45.7.1.en: Keep away from the arguing that breeds anger, and let your speech always be for edification. If you find nothing useful to say, be silent, listen, and pray that God may guide you to constructive speech, and do not depend on your mind alone, lest you fall into pride, quarreling, and strife.

45.8.s.en: (3) Jacob hears the news of Joseph

45.8.0.en: Joseph's brothers reached Canaan and told their father that Joseph was alive. The old man could not bear this surprise, and his heart almost stopped beating with joy at this news, which he never expected.

45.9.0.en: They told their father everything they had seen in Egypt and everything that had happened, and he rejoiced greatly, his spirit revived, and he was filled with joy, especially after he saw the wagons and the gifts that Joseph had sent to him, which confirmed to him the news they were telling.

45.10.0.en: Jacob expressed his joy and his longing, and that this was the greatest news he had heard, so he asked that they hasten with him to Egypt to see his beloved son, and even if he died after this, his heart was filled with joy and it was enough for him to see his son.

45.10.1.en: Do not despair because of the multitude of afflictions and God's delay in answering your prayers, for He is able to do all things and can change every circumstance, so that He lets you hear news you do not expect and fills your heart with joy. Jacob's going down to Egypt

46.0.s.en: (1) God commands Jacob to go down

46.0.0.en: Despite Jacob's joy and his longing to see his son Joseph, he could not move and depart from the land of Canaan except by the command of God, who had asked him and his fathers to dwell in it and inherit it. Therefore he moved from a place called Migdal-eder (ch. 35:21), near Bethlehem, to Beersheba in the south, where God had appeared to him before, and he offered sacrifices to God, seeking His guidance and thanking Him for preserving his son Joseph.

46.0.1.en: May you let God lead your life and be careful to hear His voice and His guidance in all your steps, so that neither your evil desires nor your material wishes nor the opinions of those around you move you, but God, who loves you and arranges the affairs of your salvation ... Seek Him many times until you hear His voice, and be confident that He rejoices in your prayers and will always guide you.

46.1.0.en: God appeared to Jacob for the last time in his life, and after this He appeared only to Moses in the bush (Ex 3). God reassured Jacob and commanded him to go down to Egypt, and promised him the following:

46.1.1.en: 1- That He would accompany him in going down to Egypt and then bring him up again to the land of Canaan, meaning the return of his descendants.

46.1.2.en: 2- That He would bless him and make him a nation and a people great in multitude.

46.1.3.en: 3- That He would care for him and watch over him throughout his life until his death, and this is what is meant by Joseph putting his hands upon Jacob's eyes, that is, at the time of death, as it is customary for those close to the dead person to close his eyelids after his death.

46.2.0.en: Then Jacob arose with joy, leaning on the hand of God, and he, his sons, and his grandsons rode in the wagons that Joseph had sent for him, and they took with them their possessions of livestock and set out on their way to Egypt.

46.3.0.en: Israel sent his son Judah ahead of him to the land of Goshen to inform Joseph of their arrival so that he might prepare the place for their dwelling. Then Israel and all who were with him reached Goshen.

46.4.0.en: When Joseph learned of his father's arrival, he hurried with his chariot to meet him in Goshen. He embraced and held him, and the two wept for a long time because of their great love for one another. Afterward Jacob expressed his joy by saying, it is enough for me now, my son, that I have seen you; if God allows me to die now, I am in great joy.

46.5.0.en: After Joseph welcomed his father and his brothers and hosted them, he said to them, I will go now to Pharaoh and tell him of your arrival, you and your flocks, and tell him that your trade is shepherding sheep.

46.6.0.en: An abomination unto the Egyptians: that is, unclean, so that they do not want to mingle with them. This was because some of the Egyptians worshiped cattle, and the priests forbade the eating of mutton while the shepherds slaughtered sheep and ate them, in addition to their hatred of their enemies the shepherds who had attacked them, the Hyksos, who even took possession of land and occupied some regions in Egypt for a time.

46.6.1.en: Joseph charged his brothers to declare, when they met Pharaoh, that they had been shepherds all their lives, so that he would settle them in the land of Goshen. By this Joseph meant:

46.6.2.en: 1- That they would be on the eastern border of Egypt so that it would be easy for them to return to Canaan as God had commanded.

46.6.3.en: 2- To keep them away from mingling with the idols of the Egyptians and their worship, which was foreign to God.

46.6.4.en: 3- So that they would not be exposed to the contempt of the Egyptians or their bad treatment if they mingled with them and learned that they were shepherds, because they despise shepherds.

46.6.5.en: Be careful to withdraw from evil for the sake of your one goal, which is the Kingdom of Heaven. If you live in the world, do not mingle with evil and do not increase your relationships with the wicked, but be content only with dealings of work, neighborliness, and the various transactions of life, so that you are not hindered or your heart drawn to their evils. Jacob and Pharaoh

47.0.0.en: Joseph told Pharaoh of the arrival of his father, his brothers, and their livestock in the land of Goshen, then he chose five of his brothers as representatives of the rest to meet Pharaoh.

47.1.0.en: Joseph's brothers declared to Pharaoh that they were shepherds of sheep and begged him to let them dwell in the land of Goshen. Joseph was not ashamed of his father and his brothers who worked in shepherding, although this was despised among the Egyptians.

47.1.1.en: Do not be ashamed of your parents, your brothers, or your relatives if one of them has a job that is lowly in the eyes of society or has a defect in any way, but on the contrary be confident in the grace of God that is with you, and as you take honor in your relatives and honor them, God will honor you in the eyes of all people.

47.2.0.en: Pharaoh showed Joseph his welcome of his father and his brothers in the following:

47.2.1.en: 1- That he would settle them in the best place in Egypt as Joseph chose, and if they wished, as they had asked, they could dwell in the fertile land of Goshen.

47.2.2.en: 2- If some of them had the ability to lead and to care for large flocks of sheep, they could be appointed over Pharaoh's own flocks.

47.2.3.en: Pharaoh cared for Jacob and his sons in honor of Joseph. This Pharaoh was one of the kings of the Hyksos who occupied Egypt in this period and were called the Shepherd Kings because their craft was shepherding, which made it easier for him to care for Joseph's brothers the shepherds, although the Egyptians despised this craft, and the king himself had flocks of sheep in whose care Joseph's brothers could share.

47.3.0.en: When Jacob went in to Pharaoh, Pharaoh felt his majesty and the grace of God in him, so he asked for his blessing, and most likely Pharaoh bowed down so that Jacob might put his hand on his head and bless him.

47.3.1.en: If you walk with God and please Him, He gives you grace and awe in the eyes of everyone, even the greatest of people, so that they seek the blessing of God that is in you and are ready to hear His voice from your tongue. So seek God and repeat the Psalms before meeting any great person, and He will give you awe in his eyes and you will influence him.

47.4.0.en: When Pharaoh saw Jacob's old age, he asked him about his age, and he declared that it was 130 years, and he commented on his age with the following:

47.4.1.en: 1- His days on earth he had lived as a stranger to the world because he was attached to heaven.

47.4.2.en: 2- His life was filled with afflictions, such as his being compelled to flee from the violence of his brother Esau, Laban's exploitation of him, the violence of his two sons Simeon and Levi in killing the tribe of Shechem, Reuben's lying with his concubine, and his sons' deceiving him in selling Joseph.

47.4.3.en: 3- That his life was short in comparison with his fathers, for his grandfather Abraham lived 175 years, and his father Isaac lived 180 years.

47.4.4.en: And at the end of the meeting Jacob blessed Pharaoh a second time.

47.5.0.en: Rameses: a fertile place within the land of Goshen, which is now San el-Hagar, and later the city of Rameses was built in it (Ex 1:11). The meaning of Rameses is son of the sun.

47.5.1.en: According to their families: according to the number of each household of his brothers' households, so the larger number was given more food.

47.5.2.en: Joseph settled his father and his brothers in the region of Rameses within the land of Goshen, which is among the best lands in Egypt because of its fertility. He took care of their food and needs, so every family of his brothers' families he gave them their needs in sufficient measure, according to the number of persons in each household.

47.5.3.en: Care for your family and their spiritual and material needs, and even for their emotional feelings and their comfort, for this is the first service that God expects from you, and give them the best you have, and God will bless you beyond what you imagine.

47.6.s.en: (4) The Egyptians become slaves to Pharaoh

47.6.0.en: The land of Egypt fainted: people and animals were exhausted by the severity of the hunger, and the land was ruined. The famine continued in Egypt and the surrounding countries, such as the land of Canaan, and there was no farming.

47.7.0.en: The people paid all the silver or gold they had and bought grain with it, and their food ran out, so they became poor and hungry in all the land of Egypt.

47.8.0.en: The Egyptians came to Joseph declaring that they were exposed to death by hunger and had no silver with which to buy, so he proposed to them that they give him their livestock and buy grain with its price. They did so and lived through that year.

47.9.0.en: The Egyptians came to Joseph the following year and said to him, we now have nothing left to own except our bodies and our land, so buy us and our land and give us grain to eat, so that the land becomes Pharaoh's and we are slaves to him. Joseph agreed and moved them from the villages to the cities, because the land had become unplanted and so that it would be easy for them to take grain from the storehouses of the cities. Thus he gave them life, and they thanked him.

47.10.0.en: The priests were exempted from slavery and from the sale of their lands, because the law of Egypt provided for giving a portion of grain to the priests every year.

47.11.0.en: All the Egyptians became slaves to Pharaoh and their lands his possession, and Joseph agreed with them that after the years of hunger ended they would sow the land and give a fifth of its produce to Pharaoh, while the rest would be food for them and their animals, and they would also take seed from it to sow the following year. They thanked Joseph greatly because he had given them life and managed their affairs. From this the following appears:

47.11.1.en: 1- The wisdom of Joseph and his outstanding administrative ability, for he came to manage all the land of Egypt so that it would be sown in the best way as he saw fit, and all the people ate, and Pharaoh's revenue and wealth increased.

47.11.2.en: 2- The mercy of Joseph, for he did not burden them with taxes and took only a fifth, so that they might live a comfortable life, eat, and have bread left over.

47.11.3.en: Ask God for wisdom so that you manage your work with excellence and succeed in the work in which you labor, so that your superiors rejoice, but at the same time be merciful to your subordinates and care for their affairs, so that all may live in peace and you may be faithful to God in all your works.

47.12.0.en: The children of Israel settled in the land of Goshen, built houses, and multiplied, so their number increased.

47.13.0.en: Jacob lived 17 years in the land of Goshen, so his age reached 147 years, which is the shortest of the ages of the patriarchs, since his father Isaac and his grandfather Abraham lived longer than he.

47.14.0.en: Put your hand under my thigh: a manner of taking an oath, as he places his hand near the loins of the person, which signifies the fulfillment of the promise in the life of the person and in his offspring who is Christ, and this was explained before in (ch. 24:2). Jacob felt that his departure from the world was near, so he called his son Joseph, because his authority and power were greater than the rest of his brothers, and charged him that after his death he should bury him in the burial place of Machpelah in which his fathers were buried, and not bury him in Egypt. This shows Jacob's holding fast to God's promise of the inheritance of the land of Canaan, which signifies the Kingdom of Heaven, for he lived as a stranger to the earth, but his heart was attached to heaven.

47.15.0.en: Joseph swore to his father that he would bury him in the land of Canaan in the burial place of his fathers, so Jacob rejoiced and held on to the head of his bed, and in the Septuagint, the top of his staff, as St. Paul the Apostle mentioned in (Heb 11:21), and this means:

47.15.1.en: 1- Either that Jacob held his staff and bowed before it in thanksgiving to God.

47.15.2.en: 2- Or that he held Joseph's staff and bowed before him in thanks for his promise to bury him in the burial place of his fathers, and this is the fulfillment of Joseph's dreams that his father and his brothers would bow down to him (ch. 37:10).

47.15.3.en: The believer lives all his days with his eyes, his thoughts, and his heart in heaven, for however much he settles on earth, he is a stranger and awaits his eternal portion. May we be occupied with this portion in thought and in subject.
